headline_marked: 6 Kushtia murders: [[ICT to deliver verdict soon]] on 4 Awami League leaders
headline: 6 Kushtia murders: ICT to deliver verdict soon on 4 Awami League leaders
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 has reserved its verdict on four leaders, including Mahbubul Alam Hanif, accused of crimes against humanity during the 2024 July Uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 (ICT-2) has reserved its verdict in a crimes against humanity case involving four Awami League leaders. The court will deliver the decision in the coming days.
The accused include Mahbubul Alam Hanif, former Kushtia district council chairman Sadar Uddin Khan, district AL president Asgar Ali, and former Upazila Parishad chairman Ataur Rahman Ata.
The case centers on the killing of six people in Kushtia during the 2024 July Uprising. The prosecution has sought the maximum punishment for all four suspects.
Prosecutor Gazi MH Tamim argued that Mahbubul Alam Hanif implemented government decisions to suppress the movement through subordinates and telephone orders.
The prosecution claims Hanif allegedly gave orders to carry out the massacre to the police superintendent, district and Upazila chairmen, and party activists.
The tribunal has recorded testimonies from 19 people, including the investigating officer. The state claims the killings were part of a planned and coordinated program to suppress the movement.
Three charges have been brought against the accused, including conspiring to kill students and the public at a meeting in Kushtia on July 29, and the murder of six people.
caption:
A verdict is imminent for four Awami League leaders accused of crimes against humanity in Kushtia.

The International Crimes Tribunal-2 (ICT-2) has reserved its verdict in a crimes against humanity case involving four Awami League leaders. The court will deliver the decision in the coming days.

The accused include Mahbubul Alam Hanif, former Kushtia district council chairman Sadar Uddin Khan, district AL president Asgar Ali, and former Upazila Parishad chairman Ataur Rahman Ata.

The case centers on the killing of six people in Kushtia during the 2024 July Uprising. The prosecution has sought the maximum punishment for all four suspects.

Prosecutor Gazi MH Tamim argued that Mahbubul Alam Hanif implemented government decisions to suppress the movement through subordinates and telephone orders.

The prosecution claims Hanif allegedly gave orders to carry out the massacre to the police superintendent, district and Upazila chairmen, and party activists.

The tribunal has recorded testimonies from 19 people, including the investigating officer. The state claims the killings were part of a planned and coordinated program to suppress the movement.

Three charges have been brought against the accused, including conspiring to kill students and the public at a meeting in Kushtia on July 29, and the murder of six people.

headline_marked: CCTV shows [[police officer helping drug dealer Raja escape]] in Dhaka
headline: CCTV shows police officer helping drug dealer Raja escape in Dhaka
summary: Footage reveals a police officer opening the prison van door to let notorious drug dealer 'Picchi Raja' and another inmate escape on a busy street.
details: CCTV footage has captured the moment notorious drug dealer Raja, also known as 'Picchi Raja', escaped from police custody in Dhaka.
The incident occurred on the busy streets of Tanti Bazar at 5:58 PM, when a blue prison van stopped suddenly.
The footage shows the rear door of the van being opened, and three masked individuals—two inmates and one police officer—stepping out onto the road.
The police officer is seen facilitating the escape of the drug dealer and another accused person from the vehicle.
The escape took place in broad daylight in a crowded area, raising serious questions about security protocols and internal collusion.
caption:
A police officer was caught on camera helping a notorious drug dealer escape from a prison van in broad daylight.

CCTV footage has captured the moment notorious drug dealer Raja, also known as 'Picchi Raja', escaped from police custody in Dhaka.

The incident occurred on the busy streets of Tanti Bazar at 5:58 PM, when a blue prison van stopped suddenly.

The footage shows the rear door of the van being opened, and three masked individuals—two inmates and one police officer—stepping out onto the road.

The police officer is seen facilitating the escape of the drug dealer and another accused person from the vehicle.

The escape took place in broad daylight in a crowded area, raising serious questions about security protocols and internal collusion.
